We're looking for an exceptional sales leader to lead the AI & Specialist Sales team within our UK, Germany & International Organisations (UKGI) business - the specialist selling engine that qualifies, shapes and wins the most complex AI, Emerging Tech, and other specialist opportunities across the public sector.

You will lead an established, high-performing team of specialist sellers as part of the wider Customer Acceleration org. You and your team will accelerates the sales cycle by bringing specialist depth at every stage, by setting the bar for what world-class specialist selling looks like across the public sector.

The role has two distinct edges. First, depth on the deals that matter most: you and your team will be on the most complex, highest-value pursuits in UKGI, bringing specialist and cross-vertical perspective that no single account team can hold alone. Second, breadth across the market: you will support account teams to build whole-of-market initiatives - repeatable, scalable plays that take a proven specialist motion across a segment or the whole of UKGI, rather than winning one deal at a time. The successful candidate will have carried and consistently exceeded quota, and built deep relationships with senior C-suite customers and partners. This is a broad leadership role and you will define the team's go-to-market strategy while personally engaging in the most impactful pursuits.

While AI is the primary focus of this team, you will lead specialist sales across the full breadth of the team's remit. That includes emerging technologies such as Quantum and HPC, as well as established specialist domains including Migrations. You will be equally comfortable setting strategy for a nascent market that is still being defined and driving a mature, high-volume selling motion - and you will build a team that carries credibility across all of them.

Key job responsibilities
- Leading an established team of specialist sellers, growing their careers, building pipeline, measuring success and closing complex strategic deals.

- Personally engaging on the highest-value or highest-impact opportunities in UKGI - bringing specialist and cross-vertical depth that no single account team can land alone.

- Supporting account teams to build whole-of-market initiatives - taking a proven specialist selling motion and scaling it repeatably across a segment or the whole of UKGI, so the team's impact compounds beyond individual deals.

- Setting the go-to-market strategy for specialist AI selling in UKGI - how we qualify, shape, and win Ai and Emerging Tech opportunities, and how we embed AI into account strategies.

- Establishing clear goals and quotas for the team, ensuring opportunities are managed effectively through the sales cycle with strong pipeline hygiene, and allocating team resources for the best use against those goals.

- Partnering closely with UKGI sales leadership and the worldwide specialist organisations to accelerate the full sales motion.

- Acting as the voice of the customer and the field back into AWS product and service teams, translating market trends and customer feedback into insight that shapes the AI and emerging-technology roadmap.

- Coaching and developing specialist selling talent of the highest calibre, continuing to grow a team with a strong brand and ambition.

A day in the life
No two days look the same. You might start on a customer escalation for a complex GenAI pursuit, then coach a specialist through deal qualification before joining an Account Manager to shape strategy with a senior public-sector customer. Mid-morning you review pipeline and quota attainment across the Migrations business, unblocking the deals that matter most. In the afternoon you work with an account team to design a whole-of-market initiative - turning one won deal into a repeatable play across the segment - then partner with worldwide specialist and product teams to bring the field's voice back into the service roadmap.

We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Are you a passionate problem solver with a talent for unravelling intricate technical challenges? Do you flourish in an environment that demands innovation, resilience, and the ability to build and maintain robust services? If so, we have an exciting opportunity for you within the Infrastructure Reliability Engineering Organisation (IREO) team.

You’ll have the privilege of being a valued member of an exceptional team, thriving in a dynamic and enthusiastic environment that combines dedication and enjoyment. A day in the life of a support engineer looks something like this:
• Dive deep to pinpoint the underlying causes of customer-related issues, providing valuable assistance in escalations when necessary.
• Apply Linux expertise to troubleshoot, innovate solutions, and resolve technical issues.
• Efficiently managing ticket queues for both our internal team and partner service teams ensuring service level agreements (SLAs) are met.
• Leading the team to enhance operational efficiency by analysing root causes, trends and developing metrics, procedures, tools and documentation.
• Engaging with internal service teams to contribute to company-wide initiatives, including tasks such as patching, operating system migrations, and code updates.
• Working with various internal software development teams to actively enhance systems and services within the team’s scope.
• Collaborating closely with experienced engineers and actively engaging in knowledge-sharing sessions with the team.
• Allocated personal development time for mastering new programming languages, honing software development skills, and crafting services to enrich your career growth.

At Amazon Web Services (AWS), you will get hands-on experience with tools and services that exist outside the scope of native AWS products. This presents an exciting opportunity to engage with systems you might not encounter otherwise, allowing you to gain invaluable experience in infrastructure development.

Career Growth
We hire and develop the best and champion the relentless pursuit of self-improvement. We understand the significance of training, and upon joining the team, you will undergo our comprehensive training programme. This programme is designed to provide you with a deeper understanding of the tools we utilise and the service teams we collaborate with.
Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.
Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

About the team
Here at AWS, we embrace our differences. We are committed to furthering our culture of inclusion. We have ten employee-led affinity groups, reaching 40,000 employees in over 190 chapters globally. We have innovative benefit offerings, and we host annual and ongoing learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences. Amazon’s culture of inclusion is reinforced within our 16 Leadership Principles, which remind team members to seek diverse perspectives, learn and be curious, and earn trust.

excluded_nonbusiness_jobs.description:
Reverse Logistics Services (RLS) exists to make returns effortless and reliable for every Amazon customer — no matter which store or partner they walk into. In the UK, we deliver that experience across a large network of partner and carrier locations, through convenience-led options such as Label-Free, Box-Free (LFBF) drop-off and every other way a customer can return an item in-store.

The ISX Partner Coach, UK owns the quality and consistency of that experience across the territory of the UK network. Because returns run through thousands of independent partner sites, the experience can vary widely from one location to the next — and the core of this role is closing that gap. You will get into the field, see how returns actually happen at partner locations, coach partners and their teams to the standard customers expect, and use data to focus your time on the sites that need help most. Your mission is holistic: improving in-store returns execution across all return types, so a customer's experience is just as good at the busiest location as it is at the smallest.

This role is grounded in field execution. Alongside coaching individual sites, you will help deploy the network-wide improvements that lift the UK network as a whole: in-store signage and wayfinding, store supplies and replenishment, associate support and training, and the tools partners rely on to process returns. You will feed what you learn in the field back into these programs, work with internal teams to roll them out in the UK, and surface local insight that helps improve the broader EU standards — turning on-the-ground observation into lasting improvement.

This is also a founding, build-from-scratch role. You'll be one of the first ISX Partner Coaches in the UK and one of the earliest members of the EU field team, reporting to the EU ISX Senior Manager. There's no established playbook yet — you'll help create it. We're looking for someone with drive, comfort with ambiguity, and the judgment to focus on the work that matters most while the team, tools, and standards are still taking shape.

Key job responsibilities
Deliver the in-store returns experience across the assigned UK territory, ensuring returns are fast, easy, and reliable across all return types.

Get into the field and coach. Visit partner locations, observe how returns are handled, and coach partner teams to Amazon's standards for speed, accuracy, and customer experience.

Use data to prioritize. You can't be everywhere — use performance data to find the locations and partners falling furthest behind and focus where you improve the customer experience most.

Drive measurable improvement on the metrics that define a great returns experience: speed of service, processing reliability, customer satisfaction, and site readiness.

Deploy network-wide improvements. Support the rollout of scalable programs — in-store signage and wayfinding, supplies and replenishment, associate support and training, and returns-processing tools — adapting them for local sites.

Manage performance to resolution. Follow a structured coaching and follow-up cycle for underperforming sites, and partner with the right internal teams (Business Partnerships for retail, Transportation for carriers) when issues need escalation.

Help build the foundation. As a founding team member, contribute to how the EU field team audits, coaches, and reports, and feed your field insights into monthly ISX reporting.

A day in the life
Reverse Logistics Services (RLS) owns Amazon's returns journey end-to-end — everything after a customer decides to send something back, until delivery at our FC. Our purpose is simple but hard: make returns effortless and reliable for every customer, across one of retail's largest reverse-logistics networks.

Within RLS, the In-Store Experience (ISX) team focuses on where returns meet the real world — the thousands of partner and carrier locations customers walk into. Working from the field, we close the gap between the best and worst locations, coach partners to a standard customers can count on, and build mechanisms that lift the whole network.

excluded_nonbusiness_jobs.description:
We are seeking an Internal Auditor to join the Worldwide Amazon Stores Internal Audit team. Stores is one of the largest areas of Amazon’s business and continues to grow rapidly, spanning fulfillment centers, supply chain, logistics, transportation, and physical stores. This is a high-visibility opportunity where you will gain broad exposure across the business, contribute to audits that matter, and help drive meaningful improvements. Our team is cross-functional, and you will work on a wide range of operational and technical audits. You should be comfortable working independently on assigned audit work while also being a strong teammate.

In this role, you will execute audit procedures and testing based on defined audit scope and objectives. You will dig into the details of processes and controls, build an understanding of complex operational and technical environments, and help identify control gaps and process improvement opportunities related to operations, regulatory compliance, organisation, policy, and technology. You will work closely with Audit Managers and senior auditors, and interact with engineers and business leaders to gather information, test controls, and document results clearly and accurately. You will manage your own deliverables across multiple audits at the same time.

We are not looking for someone who only documents issues. You should be able to clearly explain what you observe, why it matters, and how it impacts the business. You will contribute to well-written findings and reporting, support the prioritisation of issues in line with business objectives and regulatory expectations, and over time build confidence working with stakeholders to align on practical solutions and help verify that issues are addressed appropriately.

Key job responsibilities
- Executes assigned audit tasks and test steps on well defined components of audits within agreed timelines, under guidance from more senior auditors.
- Works effectively as a contributor within the audit team, collaborating with peers and supporting Audit Managers and senior auditors.
- Applies analytical thinking, including the use of data analytics and audit tools, to identify control gaps, process inefficiencies, and exceptions in assigned audit areas.
- Executes defined data analysis procedures to support testing, validate populations, and identify anomalies, escalating questions as needed.
- Dives deep into assigned processes and controls to ensure testing is complete, accurate, and well documented.
- Delivers high quality work by validating test results, reconciling data where applicable, and maintaining strong attention to detail.
- Supports the development of clear and concise workpapers and draft findings that explain the issue and business impact.
- Escalates issues, roadblocks, and priority conflicts appropriately and seeks direction when needed.
- Communicates clearly and professionally, both verbally and in writing, with audit team members and stakeholders.
- Demonstrates curiosity and willingness to learn by building knowledge of audit practices, controls, data analytics, and assigned business domains.

About the team
Our team focuses on the Worldwide Amazon Stores Business, which includes all the processes and systems from the time the customer “clicks” to order a product to the item being delivered or returned and everything in between. Our audit universe is inventory procurement, fulfillment center operations, customer fulfillment, customer delivery experience, supply chain optimization, transportation, Amazon Logistics, robotics, health, safety, and environmental compliance, customer service, and unique delivery channels like WFM, Prime Now, Fresh and Pantry.

excluded_nonbusiness_jobs.description:
This is not your typical Learning Experience Designer (LXD) role. We are building the future of vendor education at Amazon - designing AI-native learning solutions that help thousands of vendors across Europe succeed on our platform. Our team doesn't build courses and hope vendors find them. We design intelligent, data-informed learning experiences embedded directly where vendors work - surfacing the right content, to the right vendor, at the right moment.

The LXD will work at the intersection of learning theory, instructional design, product thinking, and AI to create solutions that scale across multiple marketplaces and languages. Day to day, you will design and produce learning content (eLearning modules, videos, playlists, job aids) while increasingly shaping how that content is structured, delivered, and personalized through AI and platform integration. You will use vendor to inform what you design and measure whether it works.

We need someone who is curious about technology, comfortable with ambiguity, and energized by solving for learning gaps in ways that have not existed before. If you want to push e-learning modules through a traditional ADDIE pipeline each week, this isn't the role for you. If you want to design AI-native learning solutions that directly reduce vendor errors, accelerate their growth, and drive measurable business impact then read on.



Key job responsibilities
- Design and develop across multiple modalities: eLearning, video, job aids, playlists, and in-tool embedded content.
- Apply design judgment to determine the right solution for each problem. Recommend the format, modality, and channel that will drive the most impact with the least friction
- Translate complex vendor processes into clear, accessible learning content for a diverse, multilingual audience across European marketplaces
- Design learning products: embedded contextual guidance, adaptive paths, modular components, not just standalone courses.
- Work with AI as the default, not an add-on. Use generative AI to draft, iterate, localize, and scale content.
- Structure content for machine consumption: create modular assets with clear metadata so they can be surfaced by AI tools, chatbots, and platform surfaces.
- Experiment continuously. Evaluate emerging AI tools and workflows and bring proposals to the team.
- Inform requirements for how educational content integrates with Vendor Central, working with central tech teams.
- Manage multiple concurrent projects from needs analysis through launch and iteration.
- Facilitate scoping sessions with SMEs. Drive efficient review cycles that maintain quality without unnecessary bottlenecks.
- Drive adoption, continuous improvement and maintain content freshness across your portfolio. Own the quality bar for everything you ship.

A day in the life
Your morning starts with a product team working session - a vendor workflow is driving errors and you work backwards from the data to define the right intervention and where it needs to live. Then you're building: scripting a video with AI, structuring a learning path, designing an in-context prompt. Later, you review adoption data on your portfolio and propose iterations. Between builds, you coordinate with partner teams to integrate content where vendors actually work -chatbots, Vendor Central pages, onboarding flows.

About the team
The vision of the EU Stores Learning Team is to be the most trusted partner in functional capability development, building the best negotiators in Retail and vendors who are able to expertly self-serve through intelligent learning solutions. We have a diverse team working across both internal (employee) and external (vendor) populations to drive tangible business results though educational solutions

The Localization Producer will manage the creative localization pipeline — from asset acquisition and creative adaptation through casting, recording, mix, QC, and final delivery — ensuring that localized assets maintain the creative intent and quality bar of the original campaign while resonating with local audiences. They will serve as the primary creative production liaison between Amazon Studios Production, Studios Marketing, and third-party localization vendors, providing creative oversight and technical expertise across dubbing, subtitling, artwork adaptation, and versioning workflows. Creative Asset Development & Production Oversight

Vendor Management & Creative Partner Coordination

Production Pipeline & Asset Management

Identify creative production efficiencies and cost optimization opportunities without compromising quality

Collaborate with Finishing Producers to align on source asset readiness and localization timelines
Coordinate with regional marketing POCs to incorporate local market creative insights and cultural adaptation requirements

Join an innovative team that delivers tailored products and services to protect our customers and business operations. The mission of Amazon World Wide Operations Security (WWOS) is to mitigate security and operational risks and impact to our associates, operations, assets, and brand.
Amazon is looking for a Meteorologist (London based) in support of our Global Risk and Resilience team.

The Meteorologist, a member of the WWOS Meteorology team, will be an individual contributor (IC) responsible for (1) producing tactical meteorological forecast products in support of logistics operations across the EU and Rest of the World (RoTW) regions; (2) providing weather briefing support to operations stakeholders during large-scale disruptive weather events; and (3) end-to-end management of complex weather-related projects that strategically impact Amazon's Life and Safety, Operations, and Brand.

In this role, you will proactively identify, analyse, and inform relevant weather and climate trends and translate customer requirements into scalable, actionable solutions. You will leverage OSINT, climate radar and satellite imagery, and tradecraft to identify emerging threats, and produce written and oral briefs that help customers anticipate risks and look around the corner.

The ideal candidate thrives in a fast-paced, dynamic environment that demands critical thinking, deep-dive analysis, and the ability to manage competing priorities with exceptional attention to detail. They bring a genuine passion for delighting customers, collaborating across teams, and continuously raising the bar, always seeking opportunities to refine processes, close gaps, and deliver more impactful products.

The successful candidate must have a proven record of effective leadership capabilities and demonstrate good judgment while under pressure. The candidate will also be expected to operate autonomously, use discretion when dealing with sensitive and critical information, and apply sound business principles and data analysis to identify problems and initiate actions to address them.
This position will occasionally require working outside of normal business hours.

Key job responsibilities
• Conduct comprehensive meteorological risk analysis using advanced forecasting techniques and meteorological data systems to identify potential impacts to Amazon's operations across EU and RoTW regions
• Collect, analyze, and interpret climate data, radar, and satellite imagery using statistical methods and impact models
• Proactively identify and analyze relevant threats and trends and produce written and oral briefs, in a cohesive and concise format, to serve customers across business lines
• Monitor, forecast, and effectively communicate weather, water, and climate hazards globally, providing real-time analysis and recommendations during dynamic weather-related incidents
• Provide meteorological subject matter expertise to leaders and operations stakeholders at all levels during large-scale weather events, including support to Business Continuity Management (BCM), crisis, and security management teams
• Incorporate government-issued weather and environmental alerts and warnings into tailored weather forecast products
• Analyse weather-related trends and patterns to identify long-term risks and opportunities for improved operations resilience
• Contribute to complex weather, climate, and environmental risk assessments that consider operational vulnerabilities, historical impact data, and seasonal weather patterns across diverse geographic regions
• Engage with internal customers to understand their priorities and requirements, and collaborate with global stakeholders to establish clear operational risk thresholds and escalation paths that protect people, operations, assets, and brand
• Contribute to the development and implementation of crisis management protocols and response procedures across multiple organizational levels
• Design and implement automated solutions to streamline threat monitoring, risk assessment, and notification processes
• Develop and/or maintain advanced weather monitoring systems and information dashboards to track potential threats to Amazon facilities and operations
• Train and advise teams across the organization on weather-related risk identification, preparation, and crisis management


A day in the life
A typical day starts with reviewing overnight Kepler forecasts and any government weather alerts that have come in across EU markets. If Umbrella's automated run has fired overnight, we confirm protections deployed correctly and check for silent failures or coverage gaps. On a quiet day, the focus shifts to protection efficiency analysis, SOP development, or progressing the quarterly rules review cycle. On a live day, it moves fast. WWOS Met delivers an activation recommendation, we stand up the SEM within 60 minutes, populate the tracker, pull lanes via PRECOG, schedule the call, and start coordinating across EUCX, NetOps, and site ops. Throughout the day there are ad-hoc protection requests from stakeholders, weather reporting to distribute, and the constant balancing act of protecting DEA without over-constraining speed. Tuesdays are WBR day, which means the pack needs to land by Monday EOD with the week's protection performance, attribution data, and any callouts. No two days look the same, but the thread that runs through all of it is the same question: are we protecting the right customers, in the right places, at the right time, without slowing down the network more than we need to.

About the team
WWOS Resilience (formerly BCM) is the operational continuity function within Worldwide Operations Security. For weather, the team owns the end-to-end governance of severe weather response across the EU network, from meteorological intelligence through to customer-facing delivery protection. This includes the Severe Event Management (SEM) lifecycle for weather-driven disruptions, automated and manual protection deployment through the Umbrella platform (UDD/promise pads, transit time pads, and capacity constraints), quarterly protection rules governance, proactive weather communications to CX and operational stakeholders, and site closure processes for life-threatening weather events. The team works in partnership with WWOS Met (who provide meteorological expertise and forecasting) and coordinates directly with EUCX, ATS CX, 3PCC Quality, AMZL, NetOps Control Tower, and ECFT/NFM to ensure weather-related delivery risk is identified early, protections are deployed proportionately, and customer delivery promises are maintained. The operating principle is simple: protect the customer without over-constraining the network.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is seeking a Critical Facilities Technician to join our Data Center Engineering Operations (DCEO) team.

In this role you will support the operation, monitoring and maintenance of the electrical and mechanical infrastructure that powers AWS cloud services.

AWS data centers operate 24/7 and rely on highly reliable power and cooling systems.
As a technician in this environment, you will perform hands-on maintenance, equipment inspections, and troubleshooting to ensure infrastructure systems operate safely and reliably.

You will work as part of a team responsible for maintaining mission-critical equipment including power distribution systems, generators, UPS systems and cooling infrastructure.

This role operates on a shift rotation supporting 24/7 data center operations.

About the Team

The Data Center Engineering Operations (DCEO) team is responsible for maintaining the critical infrastructure that supports AWS data centers. Our technicians operate and maintain complex mechanical and electrical systems that provide reliable power and cooling for AWS cloud services.

The team works in a highly operational, safety-focused environment, where attention to detail and strong technical skills are essential to maintaining service availability.

Ideal Candidate Backgrounds

We welcome applicants with experience from a range of technical environments including:
- Data centres or critical facilities
- Building services or facilities maintenance
- Industrial or manufacturing plants
- Utilities or power generation
- Military technical roles
- Large commercial facilities such as hospitals or airports

Why AWS

Amazon Web Services operates one of the largest and most advanced data center infrastructures in the world.
Our facilities teams maintain the critical infrastructure that supports millions of customers globally.

AWS provides opportunities to build technical skills in large-scale electrical and mechanical systems, while working in a highly collaborative and safety-focused environment.

Career Development

Technicians in the Data Centre Engineering Operations team have opportunities to develop into roles such as:
- Senior Critical Facilities Technician
- Data Centre Engineering Operations Engineer
- Facilities Operations Supervisor
- Infrastructure Operations Manager

AWS provides opportunities to develop deeper expertise in critical infrastructure systems, operational leadership and data centre operations.
Work Environment
- 24/7 mission-critical facility
- Shift-based operations
- Work with large-scale electrical and mechanical infrastructure
- Combination of hands-on maintenance, monitoring and operational support

Key job responsibilities
Key Responsibilities
- Perform planned preventative maintenance (PPM) and reactive maintenance on electrical and mechanical infrastructure systems
- Conduct routine plant inspections and equipment checks to ensure systems are operating correctly
- Monitor alarms and system performance using Building Management Systems (BMS) and other monitoring tools
- Assist with fault finding and troubleshooting across infrastructure systems including power distribution and cooling equipment
- Support operation and testing of critical systems including diesel generators, UPS systems, switch gear and cooling equipment
- Supervise specialist vendors performing maintenance or repair activities on site
- Follow permit-to-work and safety procedures for all maintenance and operational activities
- Participate in incident response and support troubleshooting during infrastructure events
- Maintain accurate maintenance records and operational logs
- Support testing activities including generator tests and infrastructure fail over exercises


A day in the life
A typical shift may include:
- Performing daily plant inspections across electrical and mechanical infrastructure
- Monitoring alarms and system status through the Building
- Management System (BMS)
- Responding to infrastructure alerts and assisting with initial troubleshooting
- Carrying out planned preventative maintenance tasks on site equipment
- Supporting generator tests and infrastructure system checks
- Supervising vendors performing maintenance activities
- Completing shift logs, plant status reports and operational handovers

About the team
About AWS

Diverse Experiences

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Operations roles at Amazon put you at the center of how things move from a click to a doorstep.

You’ll help design, improve, and run systems that connect people, products, and places, at scale. You’ll take ownership early, work closely with teams to solve real-world challenges, and see the direct results of your decisions as they reach customers every day.

Here, the impact of what you build isn’t abstract, it’s visible, immediate, and meaningful - keeping one of the world’s most complex operations moving forward.

This is where your journey takes shape through action, responsibility, and the opportunity to grow in many directions.

Key job responsibilities
- Developing in-depth knowledge of HR functions within Amazon's fast-paced operations

- Assisting with internal communication efforts to align teams across multiple countries, promoting collaboration and information-sharing

- Helping develop training plans and materials to address the evolving development needs of various teams, supporting employee growth

- Learning about HR functions across the broader Amazon organization and staying up-to-date on best practices

- Providing support to Amazon employees on a range of daily queries related to attendance, engagement, compensation, and other HR matters

- Assisting HR teams with day-to-day operational routines and administrative tasks

- Participating in process reviews to identify opportunities for simplification and automation, driving efficiency improvements

- Compiling comprehensive personnel statistics, reports, and performance evaluations to inform decision-making

- Partnering closely with business leaders to align HR strategies and initiatives with organizational goals and priorities

You might spend your morning analysing workforce data to identify trends and build recommendations for your team, then spend your afternoon supporting an employee relations case or collaborating with operations leaders on a training initiative.

Amazon's HR function is deeply embedded in the business, so no matter which project you are working on, part of your role will involve using data and analytical thinking to drive decisions. You'll apply your problem-solving and technical skills to real challenges, while developing important communication and professional soft skills through hands-on experience. excluded_nonbusiness_jobs.description:
We are looking for an experienced Operations Lead to drive operational excellence across our London studio. In this role, you will own the day-to-day operational rhythm of the studio — overseeing workflow, production planning, capacity management, and performance tracking to ensure we consistently meet our quality and productivity targets.

You will lead a team of Operations Associates, ensuring resources are in place to meet daily production goals while coordinating directly with creative teams, production leads, and cross-functional partners. You will be responsible for forecasting volumes, planning capacity against demand, and reacting quickly to shifting priorities — building contingency plans that keep production on track.

You will ensure standard operating procedures are followed, identify inefficiencies in workflow, and drive a culture of continuous improvement. You'll collaborate with regional peers, sharing best practices and delivering scalable operating procedures that maintain rigour as the studio grows.

Key job responsibilities
Lead a team of Operations Associates supporting studio logistics, volume processing, and daily production goals
Own the planning and flow of product and assets through all stages of the studio workflow, from sample intake through to final delivery.
Support annual and quarterly planning cycles for volume, productivity, and goals; track progress through continuous inspection and iteration, working through obstacles and gaining stakeholder support.
Support monthly and quarterly financial analysis for the studio.
Ensure studio KPIs are met on a weekly and monthly basis — inspecting metrics, identifying risks early, and driving corrective action.
Use data and systems to track, forecast, and plan for volume and product flow requiring stills and videos.
Drive a culture of continuous improvement — contributing Kaizen expertise, collecting and analysing data, and testing solutions for process improvements and new initiatives.
Regularly report key productivity and quality metrics to studio leadership and stakeholders.
Build and scale process-related solutions with measurable metric impact through automation and cross-team adoption.
Create and maintain training materials and process documentation to support team ramp-up and operational consistency.
Coordinate with technology and digital teams to unblock production dependencies and ensure systems support operational needs.

A day in the life
Your day starts with a production plan review and morning stand-up, aligning your Ops Associates on priorities, volume targets, and schedule changes. From there, you'll split time between the studio floor and your desk: troubleshooting blockers in real time, coordinating with creative leads, tracking live metrics against targets, and working with tech teams to resolve system issues. In between, you're analysing workflow data, building SOPs, preparing reports for leadership, and planning for upcoming volume peaks. No two days are identical — this role suits someone who thrives equally in the detail of daily operations and the strategic thinking required to scale them.

excluded_nonbusiness_jobs.description:
Join AWS at a pivotal moment in our growth in the UK. This leadership role will play a key part in our plans to invest £8 billion to expand and support data center infrastructure.

The Cluster Leader is one of our most senior management roles in the data center environment. In this role, you will be responsible for leading a large organization, managing department heads who own data center facility infrastructure including the operational availability of mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems. The pace, scale, and growth of Amazon’s data center platform will challenge you. Our uncompromisingly high standards as we continually seek to innovate on behalf of our customers will push you to new levels of creativity.

At this level, Amazon is unique in that we seek experienced senior leaders who have evolved to be highly strategic in their approach to managing their business unit, yet understand how to lead large teams by example who will not hesitate to roll up their sleeves when tactical needs dictate it.

The ideal candidate for this role will have experience of leading large organizations, with data center experience not required to be successful in this role.

If you are passionate about Customer Experience, think and act globally and want to contribute to the operational excellence of Amazon data centers. This may be the challenge you’ve been looking for!

Key job responsibilities
- Drive safety culture and security initiatives across multiple data center facilities
- Develop and implement operational strategies that align with AWS's global standards while addressing cluster requirements
- Oversee capacity planning, delivery, and growth strategies to meet customer demand
- Direct engineering operations across multiple data centers
- Manage complex multi-stakeholder coordination requirements with internal teams, vendors, and local authorities
- Champion inclusion, diversity, and equity initiatives within the regional organization
- Implement sustainability programs and ensure environmental compliance across all facilities
- Oversee financial performance, budget planning, and cost optimization initiatives
- Drive continuous improvement in operational metrics, efficiency, and service delivery
- Hiring, managing, and developing the operations management team

About the team
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.
You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Our Playback Operations Systems Group is looking for a motivated, results-oriented, dedicated and operationally focused System Development Engineer to support the fast-evolving and expanding device automation systems, that support our live events and 24/7 linear operations. The Playback Ops Systems Group build and maintain reliable, high performance customer experience monitoring tooling and infrastructure. Are you a strategic communications professional with a passion for policy, media relations, and creative campaigning?

Amazon is looking for a Policy Communications Manager to join our UK Stores & Corporate Communications team, based in London.

In this role, you will develop and execute communications strategies that support Amazon's policy objectives in the UK, helping to ensure that debates about legislation and regulation are informed and accurate. The successful candidate will be a key member of the UK Comms team, reporting to the UK Head of Corporate Communications.

You will work at the intersection of public policy, media relations, litigation and corporate reputation – translating complex policy topics into compelling narratives for policymakers, media, third parties and the public. You will develop integrated campaigns across earned, owned, and paid channels, build relationships with policy-focused media and commentators, and support Amazon's engagement with key stakeholders in Westminster, Whitehall, and beyond.

This role requires an experienced, creative, and versatile communicator who demonstrates sound judgement under pressure, excellent writing and storytelling skills, and an ability to engage both policy and business audiences. You will collaborate closely with colleagues across Public Policy, Legal, and business teams to align communications strategies with Amazon's broader objectives.

Key job responsibilities
• Develop and execute proactive communications campaigns that support Amazon's UK policy priorities across earned, owned, paid, and social media channels.
• Build and maintain relationships with policy-focused media, commentators, and non-traditional media to shape coverage of issues relevant to Amazon.
• Craft compelling narratives, messaging, and content (including media materials, briefing documents, owned articles, social media content and executive communications) that translate complex policy topics for target audiences.
• Provide strategic communications counsel to Public Policy colleagues and business leaders on policy-related issues, regulatory developments, and reputational opportunities.
• Monitor the UK political and regulatory landscape to identify emerging issues and proactively develop communications responses and campaigns.
• Support issues management and reactive media handling on policy-related topics, working collaboratively with the wider UK communications team and international colleagues.

About the team
The UK Stores & Corporate Communications team is made up of communications professionals focusing on the Amazon Store, as well as corporate campaign topics and internal comms. We work in partnership with business teams, specialist PR topic teams, and colleagues from marketing, owned content, social, and public policy.

Our policy communications work sits within the broader International Stores & Corporate Communications (ISCC) organisation, which is responsible for Amazon communications in 29 countries outside of the U.S. and China. We use communication to ensure debates about legislation and regulation are informed and accurate, and we work to protect and enhance Amazon's reputation with policymakers and regulators. Our work is guided by Amazon's Leadership Principles and a commitment to creative, data-driven storytelling.

Amazon spent decades building one of the best supply chains in the world to run its own business, moving, storing, and delivering products fast and reliably. Amazon Supply Chain Services (ASCS) now opens that same network up to other businesses, so any company can use Amazon's multimodal ground and air freight, warehousing, distribution & fulfillment, and parcel shipping to run their own operations. Think of it like what AWS did for cloud computing, but for supply chain, and it is just getting started.

We are looking for a driven, results-oriented Principal Integrated Marketing Manager to join the Amazon Supply Chain Services team. You will have the opportunity to define and drive the integrated marketing strategy for current and future Amazon supply chain solutions. The successful candidate will be expected to think and act both strategically and tactically: from the creation of plans, to the brass tacks of execution. She or he will be a self-starter, comfortable with ambiguity in a fast-paced and ever-changing environment, and able to think big while paying careful attention to detail. This is a highly visible position that will interact at all levels of the organization.

The ideal candidate will be an experienced B2B marketer, who can think strategically and execute flawlessly. If you’re looking to join a dynamic, growing team in a high-impact role, bring your insight, imagination, and a healthy disregard for the impossible to this challenging and growing business. You bring strong analytical skills, strong organizational and project management skills, and you have a track record of successfully navigating matrixed organizations, influencing without direct authority. You have a high level of comfort navigating ambiguity, a passion for scaling learnings beyond your immediate team, and the ability to investigate complex challenges and effectively influence cross-functional stakeholders. You work backwards from the customer, apply innovative thinking, and dive deep to identify and mitigate gaps.


Key job responsibilities
• Own end-to-end campaign architecture. Define audience, channel mix, sequencing, and timing for integrated campaigns spanning performance marketing, field marketing, content marketing, events, and experimental tactics to activate customers.
• Align marketing to GTM motions. Partner with sales leadership as the single point of accountability for building campaign playbooks tuned to distinct motions ensuring marketing investment maps to active sales priorities.
• Build repeatable, durable playbooks. Author and scale standardized playbooks for new ASCS service launches and evergreen growth motions, avoiding reinventing campaign approaches and ensuring campaign quality every time.
• GTM orchestration. Maintain a campaign calendar that sequences tactics for compounding effect (e.g., event → content nurture → digital retargeting → sales handoff) and prevents duplication across channel teams.
• Define integrated measurement. Build a cross-channel KPI and reporting framework that evaluates performance holistically, and drive retrospectives that turn attribution data into concrete optimization.
• Manage marketing budget, budget tracking tools and build mechanisms with key stakeholder and channel owners to track investments and ROI.

The ASPI Energy & Utilities Specialist Team is seeking an experienced and deeply technical Data and AI Solutions Architect to accelerate AI adoption across Global energy and power customers. This is a builder-first role. You will prototype, architect, and deliver production-grade AI solutions spanning agentic platforms, developer tools (Claude Code, Codex, Kiro), governance, and cybersecurity. You will bridge the gap between frontier AI capabilities (large language models, multimodal foundation models, retrieval-augmented generation, speech-to-speech models) and real-world energy environments, from operational productivity to developer platforms and real-time trading and utility operations centers.

As a trusted technical advisor, you will guide energy engineering and product teams through designing AI-native products and services: agentic systems for product development and real time operations, AI assistants that automate technician dispatch, and GenAI copilots for operations. You will work backwards from customer outcomes to define reference architectures that combine AWS AI services (Amazon Bedrock, AgentCore, Continuum, and others) with partner and open-source components in regulated industry deployments.

This role requires someone who builds. You will write code, construct proof-of-concept implementations, contribute to open-source projects, and develop reusable blueprints that accelerate GenAI adoption across the energy vertical. You will influence AWS product roadmaps by translating customer requirements into feature requests and working directly with service teams. You will publish your work through whitepapers, blog posts, reference architectures, and conference presentations.

The ideal candidate combines deep analytics and AI expertise with a passion for shipping AI products in complex, regulated environments. You are equally comfortable whiteboarding transformer architectures with ML engineers, designing multi-turn agentic workflows, and understanding the operational realities of energy customers.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and deliver generative AI solutions for energy customers across multiple industry domains.

- Architect end-to-end AI pipelines integrating foundation models, speech, vision, and tool-use agents with energy platforms and infrastructure.

- Build production-quality proof-of-concepts demonstrating agentic capabilities, AI developer and productivity tooling.

- Lead technical engagements with energy engineering teams on analytics and AI architectures.

- Provide strategic guidance on deploying AI agents into energy environments, addressing latency, reliability, compliance, and scale requirements.

- Develop reference architectures and reusable blueprints that accelerate GenAI adoption, combining Bedrock, AgentCore, Kiro/Claude Code/Codex, and partner ecosystem components.

- Influence AWS AI service roadmaps by capturing customer requirements and collaborating with service teams.

- Author whitepapers, blog posts, and reference implementations establishing AWS's point of view on GenAI for telecommunications.

- Drive customer growth through GenAI-focused sales strategies in partnership with AWS Sales teams.

- Build trusted advisor relationships with senior technical leaders (VP Eng, CTO, Chief AI Officer) at energy customers.

- Partner with SAs, Sales, Business Development, and the AI/ML Service teams to accelerate customer adoption and providing guidance on their customer engagements.

- Develop and support an AWS internal community of Data and AI related subject matter experts worldwide.

Amazon Logistics aims to exceed the expectations of our customers by ensuring that their orders, no matter how large or small, are delivered as quickly, accurately, and cost effectively as possible.
The European Amazon Logistics team is seeking an experienced, innovative, hands on and customer obsessed Process Engineer to drive standardization, integrating the latest technologies in our Delivery Stations and proposing new innovation initiatives.

As a member of the EU Amazon Logistics Engineering team you will be responsible for designing the new Delivery Stations, whilst also supporting process optimization and new technologies integration in the legacy sites, improving safety, customer experience, quality and cost. You will act as a key point of contact for your area of responsibility in the country you support; frequently partnering with local Operations teams as well as other operational support functions.

This position requires deep customer focus, strong self-motivation and exceptional project management skills. It will involve regular communication with customers and project sponsors at both the European and country level, and requires you to be detail-oriented and comfortable partnering across functional business and technical teams. To be successful in this role, you need to pair strong analytical skills and a data-driven outlook with strong design and innovation operations intuition.
This role will involve frequent domestic travel and you will report into the Manager of the Design Engineering team of the country that you will be supporting.

This job is located in the UK with up to 25% of time traveling domestically.

Key job responsibilities
• Drive new site designs and legacy site upgrade designs from planning to execution, including automation integration.
• Lead and drive technology integration and standardization in EU-wide programs and products, owning all layout integrations and optimizations in the assigned Delivery Stations.
• Contribute to network standardization via best practice sharing with EU counterparts.
• Provide process expertise on engineering design defining material flow, conveyor positioning, equipment requirements and real estate implications from process requirements
• Lead strategic initiatives and identify project opportunities to improve the processes and stations designs, engaging and influencing their key stakeholders.

A day in the life
Successful candidate will lead end to end design for new delivery stations and work to improve existing delivery station processes. You will work with multiple internal and external stakeholders, some of the internal stakeholder include operations, design and construction, launch and expansion, and safety.
You will produce best in class layouts for new launches, optimize the existing stations and present to leadership for approval. You will work on automation program to integrate new technologies into legacy stations.
You will lead projects to create mechanisms to improve the stations and come up with innovative solutions to the complex design issues.

About the team
What do we do?
Our team partners closely with AMZL Operations and support functions to identify, design and develop best-in-class process infrastructure and process layouts, and deliver them as EU AMZL network standards.

We are seeking a highly capable Product Manager who will help drive development of our Content Marketing operations capability, delivering automation and AI-enabled solutions that deliver at scale and impact for our customers, both cost-efficiently and effectively.

As part of EU Prime & Marketing’s Content Marketing & AI Enablement team, you will help define product requirements and success criteria for content capability tools across our production cycle; from brief intake, through creative development and trafficking, to post-campaign reporting. You will manage the roadmap for your workstream, working backwards from end-user needs to define features, manage delivery through internal partner teams and/or external vendors, run pilots with relevant content marketing teams, and iterate based on real usage data. You will be able to prototype solutions directly — using AI coding assistants and low-code tools to build, test and validate before scaling through engineering or vendor partners. You will be the connective tissue between what our users need and what our technology can deliver — translating operational pain points into product specs and holding vendors accountable to timelines and quality bars.

The role will work closely with our Creative Operations Manager, Creative team, Content Delivery leads, as well as other internal stakeholder teams and external agency partners to continuously improve content quality, volume, variation and velocity of delivery across lifecycle and full-funnel marketing.

As a new team operating in a fast-moving, fast-evolving, and complex environment, we need someone who thrives on building structure from scratch, can identify what matters most, and has the operational discipline to make it stick. The ideal candidate is a builder who gets energy from turning complex problems into working solutions — someone equally comfortable writing a product spec, running a vendor sprint, and sitting with end users to understand what's actually slowing them down.


Key job responsibilities
Capability Development
• Define product requirements, user stories and success criteria for content capability tools across the production cycle.
• Own the delivery roadmap for your workstream - prioritising based on user impact, technical feasibility and strategic alignment.
• Work backwards from end-user pain points to shape features, UX and acceptance criteria.
• Develop and test AI-enabled products and workflows hands-on - using AI coding assistants (e.g. Kiro, Claude) to prototype product solutions and validate feasibility before committing to full engineering investment, as well as identifying where automation adds genuine value vs. where human judgement is required in workflow processes.

Pilot Execution & Scaling
• Run pilots and beta programs with content marketing teams across EU P&M; gather feedback, measure adoption, iterate.
• Identify friction points in real workflows and rapidly iterate solutions before scaling.
• Codify learnings into repeatable implementation patterns that can travel across EU markets.

Cross-Functional Orchestration
• Manage delivery through external vendors and internal partner teams - holding to timelines, quality bars and agreed scope.
• Partner with Creative Operations, Content Delivery, and Creative teams to ensure tools integrate into existing production workflows.
• Act as the connective tissue between end users, capability leads, and vendor delivery teams - translating needs in both directions.

Mechanisms & Continuous Improvement
• Establish success metrics and measurement frameworks for each capability delivered.
• Surface feature requests and enhancement needs from end users back into the roadmap.
• Maintain clear documentation: product specs, decision logs, user guides, and vendor SOWs.

About the team
We are a new team within EU Marketing & Prime, focused on Content Marketing and AI Enablement. We build and scale content across all marketing channels, lifecycle priorities, and funnel stages - using AI and automation to raise the bar on speed, quality, and impact. We are designing a content operating system connecting strategy, planning, and execution and this role will help build the operational engine of the team: ensuring we are able to deliver efficient and effective work that drives meaningful business outcomes and positively impacts customer experiences.

A successful candidate for this role has experience coordinating projects across multiple teams and thrives on bringing order to complexity. There’s a universe of opportunity at Amazon.

At Amazon, your career doesn’t follow a straight line. It accelerates, twists, and challenges you in ways you never expected. From the moment you join, you’re part of something big: building products or services that reach millions and shaping how people live, work, and connect every day. This is where your ideas turn into real impact.

You’ll work with world class tools, global platforms, and systems built to operate at an extraordinary scale. You’ll move fast, experiment and launch solutions that matter. With endless opportunities to explore across teams and roles, you’ll learn quickly, apply what you know and discover skills you didn’t know existed. This is an environment designed for builders who want to see the impact of their work in the world. Ready to start your adventure?


What’s in it for you?

An internship at Amazon means real responsibility from day one. You’ll build, test, and learn alongside people who want to see you succeed, while making an impact that reaches far beyond campus.

Key job responsibilities
You will collaborate with different internal stakeholders to learn how to improve a program’s offering and its benefits for our customers. This internship provides an opportunity to collaborate with cross-functional teams, demonstrate project management skills in a competitive and dynamic business climate.

You will work on one or several projects with your hiring team in tracking open actions, conduct deep dives, provide data insights, analyse processes to identify critical points and anticipate risks.

You will support the team in recommending and executing network improvements.

You will contribute with innovative long-term and lasting solutions beneficial for the entire team.

A day in the life
Every day is different as a Program Manager Intern. You'll work alongside your dedicated mentor and team on real improvement and innovation projects that support the growth of Amazon's European network. You might spend your morning analysing a large dataset to identify operational bottlenecks, then spend your afternoon aligning with stakeholders across different countries on a project rollout plan. You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Amazon Web Services has an immediate opening for a highly motivated Project Controls Manager for critical infrastructure projects in operational data centers. Candidates should have a proven track record of planning and monitoring project performance to ensure scope, schedule, cost, and resource objectives are achieved. This role provides data-driven insight, forecasting, and governance to support effective decision-making across complex capital projects in a fast-paced environment.

The successful candidate will have excellent analytical abilities and strong attention to details to identify risks and ask the right technical questions to ensure appropriate trade-offs are made when negotiating resources, determining priorities, and escalating successfully. They must possess solid business acumen to understand and support the strategic direction of organizational goals. Strong written and oral communication skills are required to lead effective meetings with key stakeholders to drive business and technical discussions toward results. They will be fully competent in a variety of project management tools, methodologies, and techniques for all phases of the project lifecycle and exhibit demonstrated proficiency in core project management disciplines including initiation, planning, budgeting, resourcing, risk management, reporting on key metrics, quality control, and closeout.

As a Project Controls Manager, you must have deep subject matter expertise in project management, cost and schedule planning, and end-to-end understanding of critical infrastructure systems to facilitate technical trade-offs between short-term team needs and long-term business needs. You will be expected to take ownership and influence positive change, deploying and leveraging analytical data to drive quality, productivity, and cost improvements. Responsibilities include providing strategic insight across stakeholder teams during monthly business reviews and producing accurate and timely reporting on portfolio status to business and finance partners.

If you are a self-starter comfortable with ambiguity, enjoy new challenges in an ever-changing environment, are vocally self-critical, and are naturally curious, this job is for you.

Key job responsibilities
- Develop high-level operational plans, in partnership with stakeholder teams, that specify scope delivery, schedule, resource, and budget requirements. Operational plans extend a minimum 12-18 months to provide financial and headcount investment lookahead.
- Standardize the process, tooling, data, and reporting requirements for measuring key portfolio performance indices to ensure portfolio success.
- Standardize program planning data, including scope definition, cost and labor estimates, and schedule estimates, for existing and new programs to enhance portfolio planning.
- Design and implement enhanced cost and labor estimating mechanisms that incorporate actual performance data into estimate iterations via automated feedback loops.
- Create and manage goals in safety, quality, team productivity, vendor performance, and cost control.
- Producing accurate and timely reporting on portfolio status for business and finance partners.
- Planning and hosting value stream mapping events with key stakeholders to measure work throughput, identify inefficiencies, determine root causes, and develop solutions to optimize processes to support program success.
- Gathering feedback from internal customers and stakeholders to drive portfolio and program improvements.
- Applying change, risk, and resource management to adapt as organizational demands change.
- Developing new programs to support the strategic direction of the team with organizational goals.

About the team
*Why AWS*
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

*Work/Life Balance*
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

*Inclusive Team Culture*
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

*Mentorship and Career Growth*
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

You will join a dynamic, fast-paced, fun and collaborative work environment where you will help build and scale our business within both physical stores and online channels. This role is office-based at our Corporate Head Office in London, Liverpool Street.

AIS owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for environmental, safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. For over 20 years, Amazon Web Services (AWS) has been the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud computing platform. What is cloud computing? Cloud computing is the on-demand delivery of IT resources over the Internet.
The AWS Environmental team is an expanding and dynamic team that is critical to enabling AWS’s growth around the world, as well as ensuring compliance of AWS’s global operations, including physical data centers, as well as other AWS facilities, customer-facing enterprises and products.

The Environmental team has responsibility for developing and implementing AWS’s global environmental programs.
We are seeking an Environmental Engineer to support site development and environmental compliance in the London, UK region. The engineer will ensure standards and policies support regulatory operational compliance, and they will provide appropriate environmental guidance to regional operations teams. The individual will support environmental performance analysis, reporting, monitor metrics and guide the operations teams in implementation of Amazon environmental procedures. The environmental engineer will support new site development including environmental permit preparation, communication with the authorities and operational compliance. The environmental engineer will work with internal and external partners that include government entities, contractors, consultants, design, construction, operations and other key stakeholders.
The Environmental Engineer must have excellent communication skills, strong environmental regulatory knowledge including environmental permit preparation processes, demonstrated success in supporting roles for program development and management of complex and technical projects.

Key job responsibilities
• Manage and ensure compliance with local and national environmental regulations, contractual obligations, and Amazon policy; represent Amazon at appropriate levels with governmental agencies.
• Drive regional environmental programs by integrating with engineering, construction, and operations teams — fostering an environmentally responsible culture while maintaining environmental management processes and external accreditation.
• Ensure work performed by contractors, consultants, and employees is completed in accordance with Amazon standards and Environmental Regulations.
• Develop, analyze, and present environmental metrics to measure, monitor, forecast performance, and horizon scan for risk; effectively communicate insights to internal stakeholders.
• Submit time-critical environmental reports to various governmental agencies.
• Conduct thorough environmental audits and incident investigations, complete associated regulatory reporting, and develop and implement appropriate corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) in collaboration with operations and relevant stakeholders.
• Contribute/lead environmental permitting processes, including preparation, submittal, and negotiation of permit requirements with environmental authorities.

As an RME Technician, you’ll maintain a wide range of equipment and workspaces while upholding Health and Safety best practices. You'll help to keep your colleagues safe and prevent machine downtime. Our RME Technicians boost the availability and quality of our equipment and work to enhance the operational environment too.

Key job responsibilities
Proactive and preventative maintenance tasks on a wide range of site equipment
Carry out reactive repairs and fault diagnosis in a live distribution warehouse
Use the latest tools to maximise equipment effectiveness
Uphold all health and safety policies and practices
Support the development and progression of on-site apprentices
Work on continuous improvement projects and roll out best practices across a range of EU sites

A day in the life
Our RME Technicians are based on-site, so they can respond quickly to any machinery issues. You’ll carry out a range of planned preventative maintenance to our sites’ equipment to make sure it’s working safely. As an RME Technician, you’ll also respond promptly to breakdowns, investigating, finding, and implementing solutions as quickly as possible. You’ll also make suggestions for long-term improvements.

Working alongside senior colleagues, you’ll undertake day-to-day maintenance tasks and will liaise with contractors if you need external expertise. You’ll work on a range of shifts to make sure our sites are supported around the clock – allowing Amazon to deliver at the speed we’re known for.

Operations is at the heart of everything Amazon does, and reliability is one of the ways we optimise our processes. The Amazon Reliability Maintenance and Engineering team keeps all our equipment in excellent working order, from printers to fully automated sortation systems.
As a Reliability Manager, you’ll make sure that our automated systems are working at their best so that our customers get their orders on time. By exploring data on everything from control systems to sensors, you’ll maximise the availability of equipment at your sites. This role puts you at the forefront of Amazon’s emerging technology to solve complex productivity challenges.


Key job responsibilities
• Create, innovate and drive projects to deliver reliability, ergonomic, cost and resource-use benefits at European-wide scale
• Increase standardisation within the network of delivery stations, and in future delivery station design
• Optimize existing equipment/processes and support expansion of new equipment/process from concept to deployment
• Author and chair reports/ business case reviews to document project status and changes with senior leadership
• Communicate reliability program status & outputs to senior leaders periodically
• Creates strategy for long term roadmap
• Implement standards validated by the EU Engineering team and participate in continuous improvement initiatives to enhance safety and equipment availability for our internal customers, with a key focus on predictive & preventative maintenance programs.

A day in the life
Your day will be varied. Some days will be at a delivery station learning from our customers in RME, some will be working on design standards for the next generations of Delivery Stations, some will be working on a new MHE concept/design to improve Amazon reliability, and others will be managing large-scale deployment projects to our delivery stations. You would also be working with partners from Operations, Process Improvement, Health and Safety, Ergonomics, Finance, Procurement, Central & Field Reliability and external vendors to design and deploy new equipment and processes in AMZL Delivery Stations. This will require management of a large number of diverse stakeholders, strong autonomy and the ability to work in ambiguity. You will also lead regular communication with executors, project sponsors and senior leaders, requiring detail-oriented, technical and business reporting.

About the team
The goal of Amazon Logistics is to build a world class last mile operation. Amazon Logistics aims to exceed the expectations of our customers by ensuring that their orders, no matter how large or small, are delivered as quickly, accurately, and cost effectively as possible.
Our Reliability Maintenance Engineering or RME team keep our equipment performing at its best. We're a technically minded team, made up of excellent team players and guided by experienced leaders. We work together improve, troubleshoot and standardise equipment across our network of delivery stations. Everything we do focuses on reducing downtime in Amazon's crucial operations sites, so customers get their orders on time.

It is preferred that this role is located within DE (any DS or corporate office), however candidates from outside of DE, with relavent experience will be considered, and would consequently have a higher travel schedule to accomodate.
